items.title: Nick Polites Interview, 1963-10-08
items.q: It reminds me of, say, mid-thirties, Coleman Hawkins breathing through ballads sort of thing.

ctx.x: clarinet blues. Yes, yes. And it seems to sell that jazz group, but sometimes they had what, Tom Pickering on clarinet. He's a Tasmanian. Yeah, but I don't know why. But it seems to me that that's one of the things about the clarinet blues. Yes, they used to do it quite a bit more. Yes, they used to do it quite a bit. And of course, you have so much doubling of instruments down there. Like, well,

eight Monsborough is a classic example. Yes. It is really exceptional. It's just that he appears on so many records, I think, that might give you that impression. There isn't really very much doubling, except when eight does it. What all has he played since you've known him? What instruments? Oh, well, every instrument. Every instrument. He's quit the alto. He's changed to tenor. And plays that very well, as he plays most instruments. He was first known as Plunk Monsborough. He used to play banjo. As I say, he's…
We didn't really get on with Warwick Dyer. He, he doubles him. Do you play piano?
